title: First-snapshot 'defend offline work' branch pushes the WHOLE local tree, wiping every result/bonus other devices saved since this phone's cache
scenario: A director's phone was last synced last night. In the morning they open the app; boot() paints immediately from the cached role (app.js:7961-7964, setMemberRole('editor') then startApp) while sign-in and the member read are still 'Connecting…' on camp wifi. They record a memory-verse bonus or a podium. touchData() stamps meta.lastDataChangeAt = now, and saveState() sets dirtySinceLoad (1972). schedulePush does nothing because fbRef is still null (2494). Sync then starts and the first snapshot arrives. At handleRemoteSnapshot 2306-2310 localAt (now) is newer than remoteAt (another editor's save earlier this morning), so pushState() runs. lastSyncedTree is still null, so it builds updates from every SYNC_KEY in full (2589), and fbRef.update({results:{...},bonuses:{...},...}) replaces each top-level node outright. Every result, bonus, bracket, clock and announcement that other devices saved after this phone's cache date is deleted for everyone. The same branch fires with no real edit at all if a phone whose clock runs fast holds a cached stamp newer than the server's and makes any view-only save before the first snapshot.
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/demo1.js, which loads the real app.js through tests/harness.js. Local results were {a,b,c} with a newer stamp, and the server held results {a,b,d,e} and bonuses {x}. The single update written was keyed teams,results,brackets,drafts,picRounds,picSetup,bonuses,live,meta,clocks,announcements,notice, with results={a,b,c} and bonuses={}. Server-only d, e and x are erased. The existing test 'first snapshot: newer local work is pushed' only uses an empty remote, so it never sees this.
fix: Never do a whole-tree write over a non-empty server. In handleRemoteSnapshot, take a snapshot of the synced tree right after boot (loadBaseline = syncedSnapshot() after normalizeSyncedState). Better still, persist the last server-confirmed baseline under lsKey('campScoreboardSyncBase'), written on adopt and on a successful push ack, and add it to clearLocalData. On the first snapshot, compute const unsynced = computeSyncUpdates(baseline, syncedSnapshot()), call applyRemoteState(remote) (which sets lastSyncedTree to the server copy), re-apply each path in unsynced onto state, then pushState(). That sends only the items this device actually changed, per path. With no baseline, adopt the remote copy instead of pushing the whole tree. Add a sync.test.js case with server-only items that must survive.

title: Any focused Jelly component (home-card header, jelly-button, chip) counts as 'mid-entry' and freezes all live updates, including for viewers on Android Chrome
scenario: A counselor (viewer) on an Android phone taps the 'Current Standings' card header to expand it. That focuses the jelly-collapsible's shadow <button>, so document.activeElement becomes the JELLY-COLLAPSIBLE host. Because of delegatesFocus, tapping anywhere inside the open card keeps that focus, and so does scrolling. editorMidEntry() matches ae.tagName.startsWith('JELLY-') (7083) and returns true. canAdoptRemote() is then false (2243), and it never checks canEdit(). Every later snapshot goes through deferRemoteSnapshot (2316), and idleRetryTick (2279) skips it every second for as long as the header stays focused. The standings and live board stay stale with no indication until the user happens to tap outside every card. Editors hit the same thing after tapping any jelly-button, such as a tally counter. collapseCardsForIdle also never collapses the card.
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/focus.js, which uses Playwright Chromium with a Pixel 7 profile and the real index.html served read-only, a viewer auth hint and the Firebase CDN blocked. Before the tap the result was {active:BODY, midEntry:false}. After tapping the Standings header it was {active:JELLY-COLLAPSIBLE, midEntry:true, canAdopt:false}. The same held after scrolling, after waiting 5s, and after tapping inside the open card body. Only tapping the page margin cleared it. While the header was focused, an in-page handleRemoteSnapshot carrying a new result returned {adopted:false, remoteRefetchPending:true}. tally.js also showed that tapping a counter leaves activeElement = JELLY-BUTTON.
fix: Count only text-entry Jelly hosts in editorMidEntry: replace ae.tagName.startsWith('JELLY-') with /^JELLY-(INPUT|TEXTAREA|SELECT|OTP)$/.test(ae.tagName). Optionally, let viewers always adopt: canAdoptRemote() returns pendingWrites === 0 && (!canEdit() || !editorMidEntry()). That mirrors reloadWhenSafe, but the sync.test.js deferral tests would then need setMemberRole('editor'). Ship this together with the tally-closure fix below, because removing the button-focus deferral exposes that bug on every platform.

title: Tally counter taps stop syncing after the post-push re-read adopts an identical snapshot: the render-time `draft` closure is left pointing at a detached object
scenario: A ref scores a live-rankings tally game such as Counselor Hide and Seek with the +1/+5 counters. renderTally captures const draft = state.drafts[g.id] (5435), and the counter handler mutates that object and calls saveState() with no re-render (5490-5504). Each push raises RTDB's optimistic local echo while pendingWrites is 1, so the snapshot is deferred. After the ack, idleRetryTick re-reads (2288) and applyRemoteState swaps in brand-new objects from snap.val() (2348). The content is identical, so syncSignature() is unchanged and renderAll is skipped (2363), and the handlers keep their old draft. From then on every tap updates the on-screen number but not state, so saveState/pushState find nothing to send. The live board on every other device freezes. updateTallyMedals ranks the podium from the stale state.drafts (5565-5568), so Save Result (5532) can record medals from stale scores. Any re-render (another device's update, navigating away) drops the on-screen count back down and the taps are lost. On Android this only happens once focus leaves the jelly-button (a tap on blank space in #game-view). With the focus fix above it happens after every tap.
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/tally.js in real Chromium (Pixel 7) with the real DOM handlers and a fake fbRef. The fake raises the optimistic echo inside update(), acks after 150ms, and serves pruned, key-sorted reads to once(). Tapping +1 on t0 four times, with a blank tap and 2s gap each time, gave: tap2 {input:2,state:2,server:2}; tap3 {input:3,state:2,server:2}; tap4 {input:4,state:2,server:2}; then after renderAll {input:2}. The harness version (demo3.js) shows the same detachment: closure {t0:4,t1:1,t2:1} vs state/server {t0:1,t1:1}.
fix: In applyRemoteState, keep object identity when nothing changed. Save const prevRefs = {} with SYNC_KEYS.forEach(k => prevRefs[k] = state[k]) before the replace loop. After normalizeSyncedState(), if syncSignature() === beforeSig, restore every key from prevRefs before setting lastSyncedTree. As defense in depth, have the tally and placement handlers re-resolve the draft at event time (state.drafts[g.id] || (state.drafts[g.id] = {scores:{}, medals:{}})) instead of using the captured const.

title: Whole-draft pushes erase another editor's tally entries; the own-team guard makes two editors on one draft the normal case
scenario: Editor A is assigned to team t2, so canScoreRound locks t2's row and 'another editor scores this' (5444-5452). Editor B enters t2's score, which pushes drafts/<gid>. A is typing t1's score at that moment, so B's snapshot is deferred (canAdoptRemote false). A's input handler calls saveState() (5480-5485), and computeSyncUpdates writes the whole item drafts/<gid> (2545) from A's copy, which has no t2. B's entry is wiped on the server, then disappears from B's screen when B adopts. When A taps Save Result, the podium is computed without t2's score. The same last-write-wins happens with no deferral when two refs tap counters for different teams within a push round-trip.
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/demo8.js (real app.js via harness, setMemberTeam('t2')). Output: canScoreT2:false, deferred:true, pushed:{"drafts/counselor-hide-seek":{"scores":{"t0":"3","t1":"4"},"medals":{}}}. B's t2:'5' is overwritten.
fix: Diff drafts one level deeper in computeSyncUpdates, the same way live is already diffed per field. Remove 'drafts' from SYNC_ITEM_MAPS. When a draft exists on both sides, emit drafts/<gid>/scores/<tid> and drafts/<gid>/medals/<medal> individually, with null for removed keys. Write drafts/<gid> whole only when the draft is new or deleted. The rules validate at state/drafts, so deeper paths are allowed. Add a test like the existing 'a live match is diffed per FIELD' case.

title: A result saved offline is silently erased if the page reloads before the SDK uploads it (iOS PWA eviction, or deploy auto-reload)
scenario: A ref saves a result where the RTDB socket is down. pushState hands the update to the SDK, which queues it in memory only, so pendingWrites is 1. The state is in localStorage. The page then reloads before the socket recovers. iOS can evict the backgrounded home-screen app, for example while the camera is open for Pictionary photos. Or onNewVersion → reloadWhenSafe (7171-7172) reloads, because editorMidEntry() ignores pendingWrites (7087) and so treats a device with an unconfirmed write as safe. On the next load the result is still in the cache, but nothing is saved before the first snapshot, so dirtySinceLoad stays false. handleRemoteSnapshot goes straight to applyRemoteState (2317), which replaces results with the server copy and overwrites localStorage. The result is gone from every device and nothing tells the ref.
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/demo5.js (real app.js via harness). The fake fbRef.update never settles, and the reload is simulated by re-running loadState/migrateState/normalizeSyncedState and resetting the sync globals. Output: {queuedWrites:1, editorMidEntry:false, inCacheAfterReload:true, afterFirstSnapshot:false, inLocalStorage:false, pushes:0}.
fix: Use the same persisted server-confirmed baseline as the first finding: lsKey('campScoreboardSyncBase'), written on adopt and on update() resolve. A reloaded page can then compute what it never uploaded (computeSyncUpdates(base, local)), re-apply it over the first snapshot and push it per path. Also make reloadWhenSafe wait while pendingWrites > 0 (if (!canEdit() || (!editorMidEntry() && pendingWrites === 0))) so the auto-reload never throws away the SDK's queue.

title: `meta` is pushed whole on every data save, so one editor's score entry un-hides a card another editor just hid (and the reverse)
scenario: Friday night the director hides Standings for the awards reveal (toggleCardHidden → meta.hiddenCards.standings = true). The game leader is typing the last game's scores on another phone, so that snapshot is deferred. When the leader taps Save Result, touchData() changes meta.lastDataChangeAt. meta is a SYNC_SINGLETON (2524), so computeSyncUpdates writes the leader's whole stale meta (2576), which has hiddenCards {}. That replaces state/meta on the server, and Standings reappears on every viewer's phone, spoiling the reveal. Since every touchData rewrites meta, any data save races any hide or unhide.
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/demo4.js (real app.js via harness). With the remote hide deferred (deferred:true), the save pushed paths ['results/final-game','meta'] with meta = {hiddenCards:{}, lastDataChangeAt:...}.
fix: Take 'meta' out of SYNC_SINGLETONS and diff it per field in computeSyncUpdates: meta/lastDataChangeAt, meta/standingsHidden, and meta/hiddenCards/<card> as true or null for removed. Then a data save writes only meta/lastDataChangeAt and a hide toggle writes only its own card key. The state/meta rules validate at the meta node, so child paths pass.

title: An edit made before sync starts is dropped when the first snapshot wins, and dataEditPending stays true, so the device stops adopting updates
scenario: An editor on a hint-painted device saves a bonus before sync attaches. touchData sets dataEditPending = true (1990). schedulePush returns early (2494), or pushState returns early on !remoteReady (2582), and the only reset is in pushState (2594). The first snapshot's stamp is newer than the local one, either because another editor saved in the meantime or because this phone's clock runs slow. So handleRemoteSnapshot adopts the remote copy (2317) and the local edit silently disappears. dataEditPending is never cleared, so editorMidEntry() (7087) stays true. Every later snapshot is deferred and the idle tick waits forever. The phone shows stale scores and also blocks its own deploy auto-reload until something happens to trigger another push.
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/demo7.js (real app.js via harness, fbRef null during the edit, then a first snapshot with a newer stamp). Output: afterFirst {bonusKept:false, dataEditPending:true, canAdoptRemote:false}, then a later snapshot gave {laterSnapshotAdopted:false, remoteRefetchPending:true}.
fix: In handleRemoteSnapshot, on the firstSnapshot path that adopts, clear dataEditPending (and pushTimer if it's stale) before applyRemoteState, since that pending edit is being reconciled rather than pushed. The baseline-merge fix in the first finding then re-applies the edit and pushes it per path instead of dropping it.

title: applyRemoteConfig pushes the whole config back from every device whenever migrateState only healed RTDB pruning, which races with editors working in the builder
scenario: Any game saved with no rules has rules: [] (newGameShape 286, saveGame's filter in settings.js), and RTDB prunes the empty array. Quick games commonly have no rules. On every config event on every device, migrateState heals g.rules = [] and returns true (1856), so applyRemoteConfig calls schedulePushConfig (2183). Every editor device then does a whole-node fbConfigRef.set() of its copy 400ms later; viewers attempt it and are refused. If editor B commits a second builder change (a reorder tap, the next blurred field) while those echoes are in flight, an echo of the earlier version can land after B's write and overwrite it. B's builder then reverts when it adopts that echo.
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/demo6.js (real app.js via harness, remote config containing a game with no rules key). Output: {echoQueued:true, echoSets:1, againQueued:true}. Every receipt of the same unchanged config queues another whole-config set().
fix: Push only when a versioned one-shot migration actually ran. In applyRemoteConfig, record const v0 = remote && remote.version before migrateState. Replace line 2183 with if (upgraded && canEdit() && state.config.version !== v0) schedulePushConfig(). Healing pruned empties is local-only, and every device does it on read.

title: Camp-bounce loop guard (sessionStorage campSwitchTried) is never cleared, so a senior-only counselor who signs out and back in on the same tab or app is locked out
scenario:
1) A senior-only counselor signs in for the first time. The device defaults to junior, the junior member read is refused, and denyMember (app.js:7701) probes senior. Approval sets sessionStorage campSwitchTried='1' (7718) and switchCamp(senior) reloads. Everything works.
2) Later, in the same tab or the same iOS home-screen app session, they sign out. This can be a shared scoring iPad changing hands, switching Google accounts, or a director saying 'sign out and back in'. signOutAndClear (7927) calls clearLocalData (7910), which removes ACTIVE_CAMP_KEY, so the reload lands on junior. sessionStorage survives the reload, and nothing ever removes the flag (grep shows only the get at 7709 and the set at 7718).
3) The same counselor, or the next senior-only counselor on that device, signs in. Junior refuses the read, denyMember sees tried==='1' and skips the senior probe, and denyMemberFinal shows 'This account isn't on the camp list yet'.
4) 'I've been added — try again' calls location.reload(), and the flag is still set, so the denial repeats. 'Use a different account' fails the same way. The user stays locked out until the tab or PWA process is killed, which counselors won't know to do.
The revoke-then-re-add path hits the same wall: a revocation in senior (denyMemberFinal at 7741 → clearLocalData → reload) leaves them on junior with the flag set, so re-adding them never helps in that session.
evidence:
Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/demo1.js. It loads the real files through tests/harness.js makeContext and stubs firebase.database().ref().once() so the senior record approves.
Output:
- 'after first bounce: reloads= 1 activeCamp= senior tried= 1'
- 'after signOutAndClear: activeCamp= null (null => junior default) tried= 1'
- 'second sign-in: bounced? false activeCamp= null role= null'
The approved senior account ends on the denial screen. The existing test 'denied here but approved at the other camp' (tests/auth.test.js:355) only checks that the guard stops a second bounce. It never checks that the guard is re-armed after a successful approval or a sign-out.
fix:
The guard only needs to last for the single bounce-reload.
- In onMemberSnapshot's approved branch (after the `!rec || !rec.role` check at 7679, before startApp), add `try { sessionStorage.removeItem(CAMP_SWITCH_TRIED_KEY); } catch (e) {}`.
- Add the same removal in signOutAndClear, since sign-out is a fresh start.
This still cannot loop: a bounce only reloads into a camp whose probe approved, and approval stops the reload there. Add a test: bounce, then signOutAndClear(), then denyMember() with the senior stub should switch again.

title: Members drawer writes set() onto keys that may already exist, silently overwriting a member's role, name and team (including self-demotion)
scenario:
Three write paths replace whatever record is already at the key, and none of them check:
- The 'Add someone' handler does `ref(members/<key>).set(memberRecord(role, name, teamId))` (1685). The form defaults to Viewer, no team and a blank name.
- 'Both camps' also does `set(memberRecord(role, name))` on the other camp (1690).
- convertPendingMember does `set(next)` on the typed key (1519).
The drawer already holds both lists (`activeMembers`, `lists[otherCampId()]`) and never checks them. Realistic case: two directors onboarding staff on the first morning. Sam is already an editor on Team t2. Director B re-adds sam@… with the defaults. Sam's record becomes {role:'viewer'} with no name and no teamId.
- His device's member listener fires, so onMemberSnapshot → setMemberRole('viewer') turns him view-only mid-game.
- His team assignment (own-team guard, auto-follow) is gone.
- Chat and history now show his email instead of his name.
- The toast says 'can now sign in', so nobody notices.
'Both camps' does the same to his existing senior record. convertPendingMember does it whenever a seed-roster pending row is pointed at someone already listed under a differently spelled name. If the editor types their own email (add form or convert), the write demotes themselves. In the convert case the follow-up remove() then fails with 'Change refused' even though the demotion landed. The UI deliberately disables your own row ('another editor has to change your access'), but these paths bypass that, and only another editor can undo it.
evidence:
Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/demo3.js. It calls the real renderMemberList with a live list containing 'sam@example,com': {role:'editor', name:'Sam', teamId:'t2'}, captures the add button's click handler and fires it with the form defaults and id 'Sam@example.com'.
The captured write is `['set','campScoreboard/members/sam@example,com',{role:'viewer',addedBy:'dir@example.com',addedAt:…}]`, which drops Sam's name and team and demotes him. The rules (database.rules.json members/$memberKey .write) allow any editor to write any non-owner key, so the server accepts it.
fix:
In the add handler (around 1680):
- Refuse when `activeMembers[key]` exists, with errEl 'Already on the list — change their role/team on their row'.
- Refuse when `key === myKey`.
- For 'Both camps', only push the other-camp write when `!(lists[otherCampId()] || {})[key]`, so access is granted only where none exists.
In convertPendingMember:
- Pass `lists` in from bindMemberList and refuse when `lists[CAMP.id][newKey]` exists or `newKey === identityKey(authUser)`.
- To close the two-editor race, write with `ref.transaction(cur => cur === null ? next : undefined)` and only remove the pending key when `committed` is true. Otherwise show 'Already on the list'.

title: switchCamp and signOutAndClear reload with unconfirmed (offline-queued) score writes, which are then lost
scenario:
Example: a director who edits both camps saves a result on flaky camp wifi. The indicator reads 'Offline — will sync when back', pushState has called fbRef.update(), and pendingWrites is 1. The write is queued only in the RTDB SDK's memory, because the web SDK has no disk persistence. The director then switches camps (camp picker 7898, the Settings segmented control at 1731, or the footer chip).
- switchCamp (7817-7837) checks nothing and calls location.reload(), so the queued write dies.
- The result does survive in the junior STORAGE_KEY. But when they return, dirtySinceLoad is false (it is in-memory and reset per load), so the first snapshot runs applyRemoteState and replaces it with the server copy (handleRemoteSnapshot 2297-2319). The score is silently gone.
- signOutAndClear (7927) is worse: clearLocalData wipes STORAGE_KEY, the only durable copy, before reloading. Its confirm text ('Camp data stored on this device will be cleared') never mentions unsynced scores.
reloadWhenSafe (auto-reload on deploy) has the same gap, because editorMidEntry() (7072) counts dataEditPending and pushTimer but not pendingWrites. That race is realistic when a phone is refocused: checkForUpdate's HTTP fetch succeeds before the RTDB socket has reconnected and flushed.
evidence:
/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/demo4.js: with touchData(); saveState(); pendingWrites = 1, it prints 'editorMidEntry= false' and 'switchCamp reloaded with an unacked write: true'.
/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/demo5c.js: a cached result with a newer lastDataChangeAt, followed by handleRemoteSnapshot(older remote) with dirtySinceLoad=false (a fresh load), prints 'result survived first snapshot? false'.
fix:
Add `function hasUnsyncedWork() { return editorMidEntry() || pendingWrites > 0; }`.
- In the user-initiated switch handlers (camp picker click at 7898 and the Settings segmented control at 1731) and at the top of signOutAndClear: when hasUnsyncedWork() is true, either block with a toast ('A score you saved hasn't reached the server yet — wait for ☁️ Synced, then switch') or require an explicit confirm naming the loss.
- Leave denyMember's auto-bounce unguarded, since a not-yet-approved device has no pushes.
- Use hasUnsyncedWork() in reloadWhenSafe (7171) in place of editorMidEntry().

title: Firebase SDK load failure is handled destructively: a missing database script is reported as 'not on the camp list' and wipes local data; a missing SDK leaves a hint-painted editor editing a session that can never sync
scenario:
The three gstatic SDK files are separate SRI-pinned <script> requests (index.html:394-399). On flaky camp wifi, any one can fail or be truncated, and SRI then blocks it.
(a) app-compat and auth-compat load but database-compat does not. startAuth's guard (7627) only checks `firebase.auth`. onAuthStateChanged → handleAuthUser: isValidMemberKey passes, then `firebase.database()` throws TypeError. The catch (7671-7674) calls denyMemberFinal(), which:
- runs clearLocalData(), removing both camps' cached state including any offline-entered results not yet synced, the hints, and the active camp;
- clears the role;
- shows an approved director 'This account isn't on the camp list yet — ask a director to add you'.
The illegal-key case this catch was written for is already handled two lines above by isValidMemberKey, so only infrastructure failures reach it now.
(b) No SDK loads at all (`typeof firebase === 'undefined'`). boot() has already called setMemberRole(hint) and startApp() (7962-7963). startAuth's no-Firebase branch (7626-7631) just calls startApp(). Its comment says 'run local-only, view-only', but the role stays 'editor'. The editor can enter scores all session with nothing retrying the SDK. On the next good load those results are discarded by the first snapshot, as in the previous finding's demo.
evidence:
/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/demo2.js: seeds cached state and the editor hint, stubs `firebase = {apps:[{}], auth:()=>({})}` with no database, then calls handleAuthUser({email:'director@example.com'}). Output: 'before: cached state bytes= 18920 hint= editor', then 'member ref failed TypeError: firebase.database is not a function' and 'after handleAuthUser: cached state= null hint= null role= null'.
/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/demo5b.js: setMemberRole('editor') plus startAuth() with no firebase prints 'typeof firebase= undefined | canEdit()= true | syncStarted= false | fbRef= null'. A touchData()/saveState() then succeeds locally.
fix:
1) In startAuth, add `|| typeof firebase.database !== 'function'` to the no-Firebase guard. In that branch, call setMemberRole(null) so the session really is view-only, and show a retry (for example, sync indicator text 'Couldn't load sync — tap to reload' wired to location.reload()).
2) In handleAuthUser's catch, stop calling denyMemberFinal. Show a non-destructive error instead: showAuthScreen('signin', {error: "Couldn't reach the camp database — check your connection and reload."}) when !appStarted. For a hint-painted app, leave it painted with that indicator. Never clearLocalData on an exception.

title: Email-link sign-in can never sign in the installed iOS home-screen app, and each attempt spends the shared 5-per-day email quota
scenario: manifest.json sets display:standalone, and staff install the app to the home screen (CLAUDE.md and sw.js refer to installed iOS PWAs). A counselor without Google opens the installed app, picks 'Alternative sign in → Email me a sign-in link', and is told '📬 Sent! Open the email on THIS device and tap the link.' On iOS, tapping a link in Mail always opens Safari, never the home-screen web app, and the two have separate storage. completeSignInIfLink therefore runs in Safari: it prompts for the email because EMAIL_SIGNIN_KEY was parked in the app's storage, then signs in Safari. The installed app stays on the sign-in screen. Each retry burns one of the project-wide 5 daily email links (the cap is noted in the file header), so a couple of retries can exhaust email sign-in for the whole camp that day.
evidence: Read auth-email-link.js. mount() renders the email-link form unconditionally (99-122), and the success text at 117 promises it works on 'THIS device'. `grep -n 'standalone\|display-mode'` across app.js, auth-email-link.js, auth-phone.js and index.html finds no standalone-mode detection; manifest.json:7 is "display": "standalone".
fix: In auth-email-link.js mount(), detect the installed app with `navigator.standalone === true || matchMedia('(display-mode: standalone)').matches`. When it is installed, replace the form with a one-line note: 'Email links open in Safari, not this home-screen app — use phone sign-in or Google here.' At minimum, change the success text so it doesn't promise the link will sign in this app.

title: TV standings page has no way out of the denied state: a presenter machine signed into the wrong Google account is stuck
scenario: The presenter laptop is often an office or shared machine whose browser profile already has a non-camp Google account. Clicking 'Continue with Google' (the popup at 711-717) and picking that account leads to onAuthStateChanged → members once() refused → setAuthOverlay('denied') (733/737). The denied panel (320-323) has no button. Firebase persists the session, so 'reload' re-checks the same account and denies again. Signing out of Google in another tab does not sign out Firebase. The only escapes are clearing site data or adding that account to the members list. The main app's denied screen has 'Use a different account' (index.html auth-switch-btn); this page has nothing.
evidence: Read current-standings.html:310-325 (the overlay markup: the denied block holds only text) and 654-739 (startData: no signOut call anywhere on the page).
fix: Add a 'Use a different account' button to #auth-ov-denied that calls `firebase.auth().signOut()`. The existing onAuthStateChanged(null) branch already switches the overlay to 'signin'.

title: A send made while the previous one is still uploading is refused by the server rate rule, and the typed text is lost
scenario: A counselor on camp wifi picks a photo (sendChatPhoto, chat.js:287). chatSendAllowed (chat.js:164-177) sets chatLastSendAt to the time of the TAP. Compressing and uploading the ~420K-char update takes several seconds. About 2 seconds later they type a caption and tap Send. The 1200ms gap is measured from the tap, and nothing tracks a send that is still in flight (chatLastSendAt is only stamped again on ACK, chat.js:198), so the caption update is issued. RTDB sends both writes in order on one socket, so the server commits the caption a few milliseconds after the photo. The published rule requires the previous chatRate stamp to be at least 1000ms older than `now`, so the caption is refused. chatAtomicSend (chat.js:199-203) then retries WITHOUT the stamp, which the published rules always refuse too (it is dead code since the paste, and for a photo it uploads ~400KB a second time). Each refusal undoes the optimistic local write and fires child_removed. onChatMsgRemoved (chat.js:160) then rebuilds the view with renderChatView(true), which replaces #chat-input via innerHTML (chat.js:814). Finally sendChatMessage's catch (chat.js:279-281) puts the text back into the `input` element it captured at chat.js:263, which is now detached. The caption is gone, and the toast wrongly blames the connection. If the caption commits first, the PHOTO is the one refused instead ('try a different one'). The same thing happens with two texts on jittery wifi, or with two messages queued while offline and flushed together on reconnect.
evidence: Read chat.js:164-204 and 262-315, plus the rules in database.rules.json (chat/$channel/$msgId .write needs chatRate <= now - 1000, and the stamp in the same update must === now). tests/emulator/rate.mjs pins 'a second message one millisecond later is REFUSED', and tests/emulator/fallback.mjs shows that under the current rules fallback-send=false. I ran a probe with a fake RTDB whose update() never resolves (scratchpad/chatprobe.js, case D): after sendChatMessage, then 1.3s, then sendChatMessage again, there were 2 root updates in flight before the first was ACKed, and both carried the chatRate stamp.
fix: Serialize sends in chatAtomicSend. Keep a module-level promise chain, and do not issue the next update until the previous one has settled AND Date.now() >= its ACK time + CHAT_MIN_SEND_MS (an ACK arrives after the commit, so this guarantees at least 1000ms of server time). Replace the retry-without-stamp with one delayed retry WITH the stamp (setTimeout of about 1100ms, same push ids, so it cannot duplicate). In sendChatMessage's catch, look up document.getElementById('chat-input') at failure time instead of using the captured element, or keep the pending text in a variable that the rebuild restores (see the composer-preservation fix).

title: Once a channel holds 50 messages, every new message fully rebuilds the open chat view, wiping the draft, dismissing the keyboard and yanking the scroll
scenario: The listener is limitToLast(CHAT_WINDOW = 50) (chat.js:112). Firebase documents that a limited query fires child_removed for the item that drops out of the window each time a new child enters it. From day 1 or 2 of camp, General has 50 or more messages, so every new message (anyone's, including your own optimistic send) first fires child_removed for the oldest one. onChatMsgRemoved (chat.js:154-161) responds with `if (chatViewingChannel() === ch) renderChatView(true)`. That is a full innerHTML replacement of the view (chat.js:814), including #chat-input: a half-typed message is erased, focus leaves the replaced input so the phone keyboard closes after every send, chatScrollToBottom (chat.js:834) pulls someone reading history back to the bottom, and a photo button disabled mid-upload is re-enabled. This breaks the documented rule that 'live messages append incrementally so the composer never loses typed text to a re-render'. Real deletes, onMemberDirectoryChanged (chat.js:219-222, triggered from app.js:2468) and the chatReady flip (chat.js:126) go through the same forced rebuild.
evidence: I ran a probe (scratchpad/chatprobe.js, case B): seeded 50 messages into chatMsgs.general with the view open on general, then fired child_removed for the oldest followed by child_added for the new message. Result: 1 forced renderChatView(true) for a single incoming message. renderChatView(true) always rewrites view.innerHTML, including the composer markup (chat.js:814-830).
fix: In onChatMsgRemoved, remove only that bubble instead of rebuilding: document.querySelector('#chat-list .chat-bubble[data-msg-id="' + CSS.escape(snap.key) + '"]') and .remove() it, plus the preceding .chat-day-sep if that separator no longer has a bubble after it. Also make renderChatView(true) preserve the composer: before the innerHTML write, read #chat-input's value, its selectionStart and whether it is document.activeElement, then restore all three afterward. That way the remaining forced rebuilds (directory change, ready flip, subscription toggle) cannot eat a draft or close the keyboard.

title: Messages that arrive while the open chat's tab is in the background are never drawn, and are then marked read
scenario: A director has the General channel open in a desktop tab and switches to another tab, or an Android counselor switches to Messages or the Camera for 30s. Background tabs keep the RTDB socket alive, so child_added still fires. onChatMsgAdded only appends when `chatViewingChannel() === ch` (chat.js:143), and chatViewingChannel returns null whenever document.hidden (chat.js:597-599), so the message goes into chatMsgs but not into the DOM. The user may even tap the 'You were mentioned' OS notification that notifyChatMessage raised. When they come back, wireChat's visibilitychange handler (chat.js:938-940) calls markChannelSeen, which clears the unread badge. Nothing rebuilds the view: renderAll -> renderChatView() returns early because chatViewBuiltFor === ch (chat.js:803). The new messages stay missing from the open channel, with no badge pointing at them, until the user switches channels or reopens chat. In quieter channels such as Announcements, Memes and Photos that can last indefinitely.
evidence: I ran a probe (scratchpad/chatprobe.js, case A): chat open on general with chatViewBuiltFor='general', document.hidden=true, then fired child_added 'm1'. Then document.hidden=false, ran the visibilitychange body and renderAll(). Output: appended to open view = false | forced rebuilds = 0 | unread now = 0 | in chatMsgs = true.
fix: In onChatMsgAdded (and onChatMsgRemoved), decouple DOM updates from visibility. Update the DOM whenever `chatOpenNow() && chatViewBuiltFor === ch` (appendChatBubble already checks chatViewBuiltFor), and gate only markChannelSeen on chatViewingChannel() === ch. The visibilitychange handler can then mark the channel seen knowing the DOM is current.

title: A deleted or refused message pulls an OLD message back into the window; it is announced as new (toast, chime, OS notification) and drawn at the bottom out of order
scenario: Firebase documents that a limitToLast query fires child_added for items that ENTER the window. Once a channel holds more than 50 messages, an author deleting a typo or an editor moderating (deleteChatMessage, chat.js:351) lets the 51st-newest message re-enter the window on every device. A send refused by the rules (see the rate finding) also reverts locally and re-admits the evicted oldest message. Because chatReady[ch] is already true, onChatMsgAdded (chat.js:141-147) treats it as live. notifyChatMessage runs, and in Announcements (subscribed by default for everyone) that means a toast, a playMineChime, a vibration and, for hidden tabs, an OS notification for a message that may be days old. In other channels, anyone named in the old text gets a 'You were mentioned' alert. Where the channel is open, appendChatBubble (chat.js:891-907) inserts it 'beforeend', so it shows as the newest bubble even though chatMsgs sorts it to index 0. A burst after an iOS resume (one alert and chime per message that came in while suspended) has the same root cause: there is no staleness check, unlike notifyNewAnnouncements's announcementExpired guard (app.js:7045).
evidence: I ran a probe (scratchpad/chatprobe2.js): 50 announcements stamped 6h ago, chat closed, state.notify=true. Then child_removed of the newest, followed by child_added of an older message (at = 6h ago). Output: toasts: ["📣 O: Breakfast moved to 8:30 (Monday)"] | chimes: 1. In chatprobe.js case C with the channel open, appendChatBubble was called for that message while its sorted index in chatMsgs was 0.
fix: In onChatMsgAdded, after the sort, alert and append incrementally only when the message is the newest in the list (list[list.length-1].id === msg.id) and msg.at >= serverNow() - a small staleness bound such as 10 minutes. Otherwise (a backfill or replay), skip notifyChatMessage, and if the channel is open, insert the bubble at its sorted position or do the draft-preserving rebuild.

title: renderAnnouncements rebuilds the editor's open announcement composer, erasing the half-typed text (every 30s, and on each Announcements-channel chat message)
scenario: An editor taps '📣 Post an announcement' and starts typing. renderAnnouncements always does `wrap.innerHTML = banners + composer` (app.js:6977), and the composer markup is a fresh, empty <input id="announce-input">. It is called unconditionally by the 30-second tick (app.js:7361), by every chat message in the Announcements channel (chat.js:150, which includes up to 50 calls during the startup backlog and every window slide or delete via chat.js:159), and by renderAll from the members listener (app.js:2464). So within 30 seconds the text being typed disappears and the phone keyboard closes. The comment at app.js:6992 shows the authors knew a re-render wipes the input, but only the TTL chips avoid it. editorMidEntry protects remote snapshots, not these callers.
evidence: Read app.js:6942-7020. The composer template has no value binding and nothing saves or restores #announce-input. The setInterval at app.js:7361 calls renderAnnouncements() with no guard. chat.js:150 and :159 call renderAnnouncements() on every announcements-channel add or remove.
fix: In renderAnnouncements, when announceComposerOpen is true, capture document.getElementById('announce-input')'s value, its selectionStart and whether it is focused before the innerHTML write, then restore them after wiring. Alternatively, keep a module-level announceDraft updated on 'input' and render it as the value. In chat.js, call renderAnnouncements only when chatAnnouncementBanners() actually changes (for example compare a joined id list), so the 50-message backlog does not re-render the strip 50 times.

title: Unread badges go stale: channel-tab badges ignore new messages, and a message you are looking at can count as unread
scenario: (1) With General open, a message lands in Photos. onChatMsgAdded calls renderChatCard (chat.js:151) but never renderChatBadges, and the 30s tick only calls renderChatCard (app.js:7361). The Photos tab badge stays hidden until some unrelated renderAll. (2) markChannelSeen stamps seen = serverNow() (chat.js:530). RTDB's serverTimeOffset is measured at the handshake and underestimates server time by that one-way delay. Message `at` is the server commit time. When the handshake delay exceeds the delay of this message's delivery (common on jittery camp wifi), seen ends up below msg.at, so a message just drawn in the open channel still counts as unread. The home card then shows '1' after the user closes chat having read everything.
evidence: I ran a probe (scratchpad/chatprobe3.js) with serverTimeOffset = -120 and a message at = now-40 arriving while general was open: unreadCount('general') = 1. A message arriving in photos while general was open: unread = 1, renderChatBadges calls = 0.
fix: Call renderChatBadges() at the end of onChatMsgAdded and onChatMsgRemoved. In markChannelSeen, use seen[ch] = Math.max(serverNow(), the latest `at` in chatMsgs[ch], or 0) so a message already displayed can never be newer than the seen stamp.

title: Any focused Jelly element (card header, button, chip, switch, dialog) counts as score entry, so on Chrome/Android a tap on a home card freezes sync indefinitely, for viewers as well as editors
scenario: A counselor on an Android phone, or a director on a Chrome laptop, taps the Current Standings header to expand it and leaves the screen showing the standings. Chromium focuses the native <button> inside jelly-collapsible's shadow root, which uses delegatesFocus (vendor/jelly.js, class ki). document.activeElement therefore becomes the JELLY-COLLAPSIBLE host. editorMidEntry() (app.js:7072-7088) returns true for any tagName starting with 'JELLY-' (app.js:7083) and has no canEdit() gate. canAdoptRemote() (app.js:2242-2244) then returns false. Every later snapshot goes to deferRemoteSnapshot() (handleRemoteSnapshot, app.js:2315). idleRetryTick (app.js:2274-2294) re-checks once a second but stays blocked while focus sits on the card. The standings stay frozen until the user happens to tap a non-focusable spot outside every card. The same focus also blocks idle auto-collapse (collapseCardsForIdle, app.js:7193). For editors it also holds off the deploy auto-reload forever (reloadWhenSafe, app.js:7172). jelly-button, jelly-chip, jelly-switch, jelly-segmented, jelly-tabs and an open jelly-dialog or jelly-drawer all behave the same way. iOS Safari does not focus buttons on tap, which is probably why this has not shown up in testing.
evidence: (1) Ran Playwright Chromium with Pixel 5 touch emulation against the real index.html, served read-only on localhost with Firebase hosts blocked and the auth hint set to 'viewer'. Before the tap: activeElement=BODY, editorMidEntry=false, canAdoptRemote=true. After one touchscreen tap on the .standings-card header: activeElement=JELLY-COLLAPSIBLE, editorMidEntry=true, canAdoptRemote=false. I then fed handleRemoteSnapshot() a snapshot carrying a new result. 3 seconds later the result was still not adopted (remoteRefetchPending=true, focus still on JELLY-COLLAPSIBLE). (2) A minimal page with vendored jelly.js showed the same for a tap on slotted card-body text, jelly-button, jelly-chip and jelly-switch. (3) In the vm harness, a viewer (canEdit()=false) with activeElement {tagName:'JELLY-COLLAPSIBLE'} gave editorMidEntry=true and canAdoptRemote=false. The remote result was not adopted and stayed owed across idleRetryTick() calls. No test pins the JELLY- prefix behavior (grep tests: no 'JELLY').
fix: In editorMidEntry, replace `ae.tagName.startsWith('JELLY-')` with an allowlist of Jelly hosts that really hold typed input, e.g. `const JELLY_TEXT_ENTRY = ['JELLY-INPUT','JELLY-TEXTAREA','JELLY-SELECT','JELLY-OTP'];` and use `JELLY_TEXT_ENTRY.includes(ae.tagName)`. Buttons, chips, switches, segmented controls, collapsibles, tabs, dialogs and drawers commit on click and are not mid-entry. Add sync.test.js cases: activeElement {tagName:'JELLY-COLLAPSIBLE'} gives canAdoptRemote()===true, and {tagName:'JELLY-INPUT'} gives false.

title: Deploy auto-reload discards a result whose write the server has not confirmed yet (pendingWrites > 0), and the next page silently overwrites it with the server copy
scenario: 1. An editor saves a result where camp wifi is weak, or saves just before locking the phone. flushPendingPush/pushState (app.js:2585-2627) hands the update to the RTDB SDK. It sets dataEditPending=false (app.js:2594) and pendingWrites=1 (app.js:2601). The write is only queued in the SDK's in-memory queue because the socket is half-open or reconnecting. 2. Connectivity comes back. The 2-minute poll, or the visibilitychange check on unlock (app.js:7123-7126), fetches index.html over a fresh HTTP connection before RTDB has reconnected and re-authenticated to flush its queue. If a deploy shipped meanwhile, onNewVersion runs reloadWhenSafe (app.js:7171-7174). 3. editorMidEntry() ignores pendingWrites (app.js:7087), so doReload fires 1.2 s later. The SDK's queued write dies with the page, because RTDB on the web has no persistence across reloads. 4. The reloaded page has the result in localStorage. But the boot path normally makes no saveState before the first snapshot, so dirtySinceLoad stays false. handleRemoteSnapshot therefore adopts the server tree, which lacks the result, and applyRemoteState writes that back over localStorage (app.js:2361). The result is gone from every device with no error. The owner deploys often during camp (v181), which makes the trigger likely.
evidence: vm harness, two contexts loading the real app files. Context A (editor): fbRef = {update: () => new Promise(() => {})}, which stands for a socket that never acks. Recorded state.results[firstGame], then touchData(), saveState(), flushPendingPush(). Output: pendingWrites=1, dataEditPending=false, pushTimer=null, editorMidEntry()=false, so the reloadWhenSafe gate `!canEdit()||!editorMidEntry()` is true. Context B stood in for the reloaded page: I copied A's STORAGE_KEY into its localStorage and ran state=loadState(). Output: 'reloaded page has the result locally: true, dirtySinceLoad: false'. After handleRemoteSnapshot(serverTreeWithoutResult): 'result still present: false, in localStorage: no'.
fix: Gate the reload on unconfirmed writes, the same rule canAdoptRemote already uses. Add a helper `function reloadBlocked(){ return pendingWrites > 0 || (canEdit() && editorMidEntry()); }` and rewrite reloadWhenSafe as `if (reloadBlocked()) { setTimeout(reloadWhenSafe, 12000); return; } setTimeout(() => reloadBlocked() ? reloadWhenSafe() : doReload(), 1200);`. The check repeats inside the 1.2 s delay so an edit made in that gap is also protected. The update banner stays up, so a person can still tap to refresh.

title: Deploy auto-reload fires in the middle of timing: it wipes a running Pictionary lap and leaves the ref's phone unable to sound the zero buzzer
scenario: Pictionary: the ref taps 'Nose down — start'. The lap lives only in memory: liveWatches[g.id].running and startAt (app.js:3012, 3370-3374). After the tap, renderTools rebuilds the buttons, so nothing stays focused. On iOS a tapped button never takes focus anyway. A deploy-triggered onNewVersion then runs reloadWhenSafe (app.js:7171-7174). editorMidEntry() is false, so the page reloads 1.2 s later. The lap time in progress is lost and the ref sees 'start' again with no elapsed time; the code admits the in-memory copy 'dies on reload' (app.js:3221). Synced game clock: the editor's phone is the only device that buzzes and stops the clock (tickBoardClocks, app.js:3097-3104). After an auto-reload, no user gesture has unlocked audio. playAlarm calls getAudio (app.js:2765-2775), which creates a new AudioContext that stays suspended on iOS and under Chrome's autoplay policy, and navigator.vibrate is blocked before user activation. The wake lock is also gone, because it is only requested from the Start tap (app.js:5906). Result: a silent 0:00, or the phone sleeps and misses zero entirely.
evidence: vm harness, editor role, with liveWatches.pic={running:true,startAt:now-40s} and state.clocks.gx running with 4 minutes left. Output: editorMidEntry()=false and the reloadWhenSafe gate is true, so the reload proceeds. Code read: start-lap keeps time only in liveWatches (app.js:3370-3374); requestWakeLock is only called from applyClockAction 'start' (app.js:5906); getAudio is only unlocked from gestures (app.js:2895, 3371, 5495, 5882).
fix: Add `function timingLive(){ return Object.values(liveWatches).some((w) => w && w.running) || Object.values(state.clocks || {}).some((c) => c && c.running && (Number(c.endAt) || 0) > serverNow()); }` and include `(canEdit() && timingLive())` in the reload gate (reloadBlocked above). The endAt > serverNow() test matters: a clock left 'running' at 0:00 (see the zero-detection finding) must not hold off reload forever. The tap-to-refresh banner still shows, so the ref can reload between rounds.

title: Screen wake lock is never re-acquired after the app is hidden, so a brief app switch lets the ref's phone sleep through the countdown
scenario: A ref starts a 10-minute game clock. applyClockAction calls requestWakeLock (app.js:5906). The ref switches to Messages or the camera for a few seconds. Browsers release a screen wake lock automatically when the document is hidden, and the 'release' listener nulls wakeLockSentinel (app.js:3026). Nothing calls requestWakeLock again: the only call site is the Start action, and none of the visibilitychange handlers (app.js:490, 2482, 7125, 7209) re-arm it. The screen then dims and locks on its normal 30-60 s timeout. iOS suspends the page's timers, so tickBoardClocks never sees the zero crossing on the one device that sounds the buzzer and stops the synced clock (app.js:3097-3104). Separately, when the clock auto-stops at zero (app.js:3101) no releaseWakeLock runs. The Pictionary stopwatch (start-lap, app.js:3370) never requests a wake lock at all, although anyTimerRunning() counts it.
evidence: Code read: grep for requestWakeLock/releaseWakeLock finds only the definitions (app.js:3022, 3030) and the two calls in applyClockAction (app.js:5906-5907). Every visibilitychange listener in app.js and chat.js (app.js:490, 2482, 7125, 7209; chat.js:938) was checked: none re-requests the lock. The Screen Wake Lock spec releases sentinels when the document becomes hidden.
fix: In init(), add `document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => { if (!document.hidden && timingLive()) requestWakeLock(); });`. Call requestWakeLock() from start-lap as well. After the auto-stop in tickBoardClocks, and after applyRemoteState, call `if (!timingLive()) releaseWakeLock();`. Make anyTimerRunning ignore expired clocks (the endAt > serverNow() test) so a stale clock cannot hold the lock.

title: Zero-crossing handling depends on what is on screen (data-prev): the buzzer can fire minutes late, or the clock is never stopped and stays 'running' at 0:00 for everyone
scenario: tickBoardClocks only acts on [data-game-clock] elements that are in the DOM (app.js:3079-3080). It buzzes and stops the clock only when `running && rem === 0 && prev > 0`, where prev is the element's last painted value (app.js:3086, 3097). Three realistic failures follow. (a) The editor's phone locks or sleeps with 0:45 left (see the wake-lock finding). On unlock 20 minutes later, the first tick still sees prev=45000. It blasts 6.5 s of alarm plus vibration in the middle of whatever is happening now. (b) The ref starts game A's clock, then opens game B to enter scores. renderGameView replaces #game-view's innerHTML (app.js:5015), so game A's clock element is gone. At zero nothing buzzes and nothing stops the clock. (c) A render lands after zero but before the next tick, for example a reload or a remote snapshot, and repaints data-prev from remaining=0 (app.js:5941 and the Big Board variants). The crossing is never seen. In (b) and (c), state.clocks[gid] stays running:true at 0:00 on every device. Refs see a 'Pause' button instead of 'Next round', and anyTimerRunning() stays true, so releaseWakeLock never runs.
evidence: vm harness, editor role, playAlarm stubbed to count calls, document.querySelectorAll stubbed. Case 1: clock ran out 20 min ago and the element has prev=45000. Output: alarms fired=1, clock stopped=true (late buzz). Case 2: element repainted with prev=0, tick run twice. Output: alarms=0, clock still running=true, anyTimerRunning=true. Case 3: no clock element on screen. Output: alarms=0, clock still running=true.
fix: Drive the zero logic from state rather than the DOM. At the top of tickBoardClocks, before `if (!els.length) return`, for editors loop over state.clocks. For each gid whose game has a timer and whose clock is `running && Number(endAt) <= serverNow()`: call setClock(g, c => { c.running = false; c.remaining = 0; }), and call playAlarm() only if `serverNow() - endAt < 3000` and this gid+endAt has not already buzzed (a module-level Set). Call renderAll() once if anything changed. Keep the per-element loop for display classes only, and drop the data-prev crossing test.

title: Deploy auto-reload throws away a chat message being typed (and an in-flight photo send) for every role
scenario: Chat is open to every member, viewers included. A counselor (viewer) is halfway through typing an announcement-channel message in #chat-input (chat.js:828). A deploy is detected and reloadWhenSafe runs (app.js:7171-7174). For viewers the gate is `!canEdit()`, so the page reloads in 1.2 s whatever they are doing. For editors, editorMidEntry deliberately skips the chat composer (inChatComposer, app.js:7081-7083), so they reload too. The composer text exists only in the DOM input (sendChatMessage reads input.value, chat.js:262-275). It is lost, along with a photo still being compressed or uploaded by sendChatPhoto. Excluding the composer from editorMidEntry was right for sync deferral. It was never meant to opt chat drafts out of reload protection, and viewers had no inputs when 'viewers reload immediately' was decided.
evidence: vm harness: activeElement = {tagName:'INPUT', closest: s => s==='#chat-view' ? {} : null}. Output: editorMidEntry()=false. With setMemberRole('viewer') the reload gate `!canEdit()` is true unconditionally. grep shows no chat draft persistence in chat.js.
fix: Leave editorMidEntry alone so the sync behavior is unchanged. In the reload gate only, add `const ci = document.getElementById('chat-input'); if (ci && ci.value.trim()) return true;`, plus a flag set while sendChatPhoto or chatAtomicSend is pending, for all roles. The banner stays up, and the reload happens once the message is sent or cleared.

title: Chat rate limit refuses messages queued offline or sent while a photo is still uploading; the text is lost
scenario: Camp wifi drops. A director in the Announcements channel sends 'Lunch moved to 12:30', then 'Bring water bottles' 1.3s later, then 'Swim is cancelled'. The client throttle passes each time because chatSendAllowed (chat.js:164-177) measures 1200ms from the moment of each TAP, and it only re-stamps when the server acknowledges a send (chat.js:198). chatAtomicSend (chat.js:196-204) then hands every update to the SDK straight away, without waiting for the previous one to be acknowledged. The SDK queues all three. RTDB's local events show each message as sent. On reconnect the SDK replays the three updates back to back, a few milliseconds apart. The rules accept a create only when chatRate/<me> is at least 1000ms older than the server's `now` at commit (database.rules.json:154 for chat, :186 for chatPhotos, and the same at :361 and :393 for senior). So message #1 commits and #2 and #3 are refused. The retry without the stamp (chat.js:202) is also refused, because the published rules require the stamp. The two messages vanish from the list (child_removed on revert). The catch at chat.js:279-282 puts text back only into an EMPTY input, so at most one refused message is recovered and the rest are lost. The toast blames 'your connection'. The same thing happens online: a photo update (up to about 400KB) is still uploading when a caption is sent 1.2s or more after the photo tap. The caption is queued behind the photo on the socket and evaluated milliseconds after the photo's stamp, so it is refused. A caption sent while makeChatImages is still compressing goes first instead, and then the photo is refused with 'try a different one'. The test at tests/rules.test.js:243 ('the client throttle sits above the server floor, so real people never hit the wall') compares only the two constants. That assumption is wrong: the server measures from commit time and the client measures from tap time.
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/chatq.js. It loads the real files via tests/harness.js with a firebase stub whose update() never resolves (offline). Three sendChatMessage('announcements') calls 1.3s apart gave three separate root updates at +1ms, +1304ms and +2604ms, each carrying chat/announcements/<id> and chatRate/counselor@example,com. No client toast or throttle stopped them. The server half is already proven by tests/emulator/rate.mjs ('a second message one millisecond later is REFUSED'). The rules expression at database.rules.json:154 requires `chatRate.val() <= now - 1000` and `newData...chatRate === now`, so the retry without the stamp cannot pass either.
fix: Serialize sends in chatAtomicSend. Keep a module-level promise tail (`let chatSendTail = Promise.resolve(); let chatLastAckAt = 0;`). Each call does `const go = () => wait(Math.max(0, chatLastAckAt + CHAT_MIN_SEND_MS - Date.now())).then(<existing update + retry>)` and `const p = chatSendTail.then(go, go); chatSendTail = p.catch(() => {}); return p;`. stamp() sets `chatLastAckAt = chatLastSendAt = Date.now()`. With this, an update reaches the SDK only after the previous one is acknowledged plus the gap. An offline burst then replays paced on reconnect, and a caption waits for its photo. Keep chatSendAllowed as the double-tap guard. Replace the constant-only test with a harness test: with a never-resolving update(), a second send must not call update() until the first settles. Optionally drop the no-stamp retry now that the rules are published; it only doubles a doomed round trip.

title: A remote week-config change makes every other editor device write changelog entries in its own name
scenario: Points depend on config: medalCounts skips results for games no longer in the catalog and doubles messtival games (app.js:3755-3759). Editor A, in the week builder, toggles double points on a scored game, or deletes a game that has a result. Editor B's device receives the new config through the fbConfigRef listener, which calls applyRemoteConfig (app.js:2176-2185) and then renderAll(). It does not set remoteJustApplied. renderStandings (app.js:3821) therefore treats the point change as LOCAL and calls recordPointHistory(counts, false) (app.js:3871). That pushes a 'Points updated' changelog entry per affected team with byKey = B's own identity (app.js:3991-3998). The rules accept it, because byKey really is the writer. Every editor device that has the app open does the same thing. So does every editor who opens the app later: the first render uses the cached config as the baseline, and then the server config arrives. The audit log fills with duplicate entries blaming people who changed nothing. The rules-level attribution pin is defeated by the client writing on another person's behalf. The idle-retry path (idleRetryTick to applyRemoteConfig) has the same bug.
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/cfglog.js with the real files, editor role and a stub firebase. It saves a result for 'Shields', renders the baseline, then calls applyRemoteConfig() with that game's messtival flag flipped (simulating editor A's edit arriving). Result: 3 changelog pushes from device B, e.g. {team:'Ferocious Foxes', delta:7, reason:'Points updated', byKey:'editor,b@example,com'}.
fix: In applyRemoteConfig, set `remoteJustApplied = true;` immediately before `renderAll()`. This is the same flag applyRemoteState uses at app.js:2364. recordPointHistory then advances its baseline without logging, because the device that made the config edit already logged it. As a side effect, the standings pulse and the point-change notifications now fire for remote-caused changes too, which is the correct behaviour.

title: A refused send or any delete in a full channel slides an old message back in and re-fires its alert
scenario: Each channel listens with limitToLast(CHAT_WINDOW = 50) (chat.js:112). Once chatReady[ch] is true, onChatMsgAdded treats EVERY child_added as live (chat.js:141-147): it runs notifyChatMessage and appends the bubble at the bottom. In a channel with more than 50 messages, two things send the 51st-newest message back into the window as child_added. One is a rules-refused send (finding 1): the optimistic local add evicted the oldest message, and the revert restores it. The other is any message deletion by an author or editor (chat.js:353, :368). For Announcements, which is subscribed by default, every device then gets a toast plus OS notification, chime and vibrate for an announcement that may be hours old. A mention message re-fires the 'you were mentioned' alert. With the chat open, appendChatBubble puts the old message at the bottom as if it had just been posted, which is out of order.
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/slide.js against the real chat.js. It loads a ready backlog of 50 announcements, then sends child_removed(newest) and child_added(a0, six hours old), which is the RTDB window slide after a delete or revert. Result: toasts fired: ['📣 dir@x.com: Breakfast at 7:30 (from this morning)'].
fix: Track `chatNewestAt[ch]`, the highest `at` adopted so far, updated in onChatMsgAdded. A child_added whose msg.at is at or below that value is a window back-fill. Insert it in sorted order, skip notifyChatMessage, and call renderChatView(true) instead of appendChatBubble. Only a message newer than chatNewestAt alerts and appends.

title: Changelog reason has no length cap, so the rules refuse every audit entry for a bulk change such as a backup restore
scenario: recordPointHistory builds `reason = causes.join('; ')` with no cap (app.js:3984) and pushes it (app.js:3998). The rules cap reason at 500 characters (database.rules.json:95, :302), plus team at 60 (:83) and by at 80 (:98). Settings → Restore from backup (settings.js tryImport) of a backup with 15 or more scored games produces one long string of 'Game — result saved' entries. Each team's changelog push is refused, and the `.catch(() => {})` at app.js:3999 swallows it. The single most consequential points event of the week leaves no trace in the history drawer. The full junior catalog joins to 744 characters and senior to 873, and 15 games is enough to pass 500.
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/restorelog.js: editor, stub firebase, baseline render, then the real tryImport() with a backup holding 16 scored games. Result: 6 changelog pushes, each with reason.length=542, so every one is REFUSED by the `length <= 500` rule. /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/reason.js measured the full-catalog lengths.
fix: In recordPointHistory, clamp to the rules the same way chat clamps name with `.slice(0, 60)`. Build the reason from causes until the next one would pass about 480 characters, then append `; … +N more`. Also `String(teamName(tid)).slice(0, 60)` and `by && String(by).slice(0, 80)`. Optionally add a rules.test.js check that the client caps match the rules caps.

title: Members drawer offers controls on the owner's row that the rules always refuse, so the owner can never have a team
scenario: The rules make the owner key immutable from every client: `$memberKey != 'patricksimpson,fx@gmail,com'` on members/$memberKey/.write (database.rules.json:127, :334). The client has no owner constant. renderMemberList disables the per-camp switches only for `self` or for camps where the viewer isn't an editor (app.js:1394). The team select is rendered for every non-pending row, the owner's own row included (app.js:1411-1413). If the owner picks a team on his own row, members/<owner>/teamId is set (app.js:1590-1600), refused, and the toast says 'the database rules may need updating'. So the owner can never be put on a team, and auto-follow and the own-team guard never apply to him. When any other editor flips the owner's None/Viewer/Editor switch in either camp or changes his team, the write is refused with 'are you still an editor?'. That is misleading and suggests the editor has lost access.
evidence: Read database.rules.json:127/:334 and app.js:1379-1413 and 1586-1600. `grep patricksimpson app.js camps.js settings.js chat.js` finds no owner-key constant in the client, so nothing in the UI knows about the immutable row.
fix: Add `const OWNER_MEMBER_KEY = 'patricksimpson,fx@gmail,com'` in app.js, pinned to the rules string by a rules.test.js assertion. In renderMemberList and bindMemberList, treat `key === OWNER_MEMBER_KEY` like `self`: disable the access switches, omit the team select, and show a 'Owner — managed in the Firebase console' note. If the owner does want a team, relax the rule instead to allow writes only to members/<owner>/teamId and name, and keep role immutable.

title: After the device re-fetches its own write while idle, open tally/bracket/notice views edit stale copies of the data, so later taps are silently not saved or synced and medals can be picked from stale scores
scenario: A ref opens a counter tally game (Axe Throwing, Inflatable Bowling, Color Call Chaos, Hide and Seek, Pumpkin Patch Plunder). renderTally keeps a reference to `draft` = state.drafts[g.id] (app.js:5435), and the counter/input handlers write into that object (app.js:5499-5503). Tap 1 runs saveState, then pushState: pendingWrites goes up and RTDB fires its local `value` echo, so handleRemoteSnapshot defers it (deferRemoteSnapshot). About a second later idleRetryTick calls fbRef.once('value') (app.js:2288), and applyRemoteState swaps in fresh objects for every synced key (app.js:2348). The content is identical, so syncSignature() matches beforeSig and renderAll is skipped (app.js:2363). The open view's handlers still point at the old, detached draft. From then on every tap updates the input box but not state: saveState has nothing to send, viewers' live board and other devices never see it, and updateTallyMedals re-reads state.drafts, so the ranking pills stop moving. On Save Result (app.js:5527-5545) the scores come from the stale copy but the medal picks are auto-filled from the out-of-date state, so the wrong teams can get medals. Any later renderAll (another editor's change, or the clock reaching 0:00 at app.js:3101) puts the inputs back to the stale values and the taps are lost. In Chrome on Android a focused counter jelly-button holds off the re-fetch until the ref taps elsewhere; after that, every tap is lost and focus blocks any re-render. The same thing happens to brackets: `b` from app.js:5784 goes stale, so the first chip, winner or undo tap after each idle re-fetch does nothing, while touchData still shows the celebration. It also hits the notice builder: `n` from settings.js:1279 goes stale and field edits disappear before Post. This came in with the 2026-07-25 idle re-fetch, after camp week, so it has never run at a live camp.
evidence: Ran detach.js in the scratchpad. It loads the real app through tests/harness.js, uses a fake RTDB that prunes and sorts keys and fires the local echo synchronously, calls the real renderTally counter handler, then runs flushPendingPush + idleRetryTick: 'tap 1: input shows 1 | state t1 = 1 | server t1 = 1', 'tap 2: input shows 2 | state t1 = 1 | server t1 = 1', ... 'tap 4: input shows 4 | state t1 = 1 | server t1 = 1', and renderAll was never called by the echo. bracket.js runs the real renderBracketRound1 chip handlers: after the first chip tap and an idle re-fetch, the second chip tap leaves selectedPair at ["t0"] even though renderAll ran.
fix: In applyRemoteState, save the current objects before merging (`const prevRefs = SYNC_KEYS.map((k) => state[k]);`). After normalizeSyncedState and re-attaching the Pictionary words, if `syncSignature() === beforeSig`, put them back (`SYNC_KEYS.forEach((k, i) => { state[k] = prevRefs[i]; })`) before setting lastSyncedTree. The content is identical, so this changes nothing else, and any real change still goes through renderAll, which rebuilds the handlers. For extra safety, have the renderTally and bracket handlers look up `state.drafts[g.id]` / `state.brackets[g.id]` when the event fires instead of holding a reference. Add a sync.test case: keep a reference to state.drafts.g, apply an identical echo with applyRemoteState, and assert the reference is still state.drafts.g.

title: Tally drafts are written as one whole object per game, so two editors scoring the same game (the setup the own-team guard requires) wipe each other's team scores
scenario: Under the own-team guard (canScoreRound, app.js:128; renderTally locks the row at app.js:5446) an editor can't score their own team, so another editor has to, at the same time on the same tally game. 'drafts' is in SYNC_ITEM_MAPS (app.js:2520), so computeSyncUpdates sends the whole `drafts/<gid>` object whenever any team's score changes. Editor B starts typing team t0's score; the focused input makes canAdoptRemote() false, so B holds off on A's updates. Meanwhile editor A enters t1=7 and t2=4. When B leaves the field, flushPendingPush sends B's out-of-date draft `{scores:{t0:'12'}}` over the server copy. A's scores are gone on the server, and A's device takes B's version on its next idle re-fetch. This isn't a narrow race: holding off while focused guarantees B's push is stale. Chrome on Android makes it worse: editorMidEntry treats any focused `JELLY-*` element as mid-entry (app.js:7083), and a tapped counter jelly-button keeps focus, so a ref who keeps tapping counters holds off on other editors' updates the whole time and every push reverts them. The same whole-object write applies to `brackets/<gid>` when two editors hand a bracket back and forth.
evidence: Ran twoeditors.js: two harness contexts sharing one fake RTDB. Output: 'server after A: {"axe-throwing":{"scores":{"t1":"7","t2":"4"}}}', 'B has adopted A? {}', 'B pushed: {"drafts/axe-throwing":{"scores":{"t0":"12"},"medals":{}}}', 'server after B: {"axe-throwing":{"scores":{"t0":"12"}}}', 'A now shows: {"t0":"12"}'. The rules (database.rules.json state.drafts) only validate the drafts branch itself, so deeper per-team paths are allowed.
fix: Take 'drafts' out of SYNC_ITEM_MAPS and diff it one level deeper in computeSyncUpdates, the way `live` already is. If a draft is new or deleted, write or null `drafts/<gid>` whole. Otherwise, for f in ['scores','medals'], write `drafts/<gid>/<f>/<key>` for each changed leaf and null for each removed one, with no overlapping paths. Add a sync.test case like 'a live match is diffed per FIELD': one changed team score must produce only `drafts/g/scores/t1`. Optionally narrow the editorMidEntry focus check to form-entry hosts (JELLY-INPUT, JELLY-TEXTAREA, JELLY-SELECT) instead of every `JELLY-` tag, so a focused counter button doesn't hold off updates.

title: Week-builder saves send the whole config from a stale copy, wiping another editor's newer changes even when this device already has the newer version waiting
scenario: Editor B opens 'Axe Throwing' in the game editor and edits its headline or rules. builderDirty() makes editorMidEntry() true, so when editor A saves a new rain-day game, B's config listener stores A's version in pendingRemoteConfig (app.js:2447) instead of applying it. B taps Save: saveGameDraft (settings.js:716) splices B's game into B's stale state.config (settings.js:799), and saveConfig calls pushConfig, which overwrites the whole config node (app.js:2223). A's new game disappears from the server and from A's screen. B's own echo then replaces the stored version, so A's change is gone for good. Any result A already saved for that game becomes orphaned: medalCounts drops it from the standings, but current-standings.html:435 still counts it, so the TV and the app disagree. The same happens with the Days tab handlers (settings.js:912-966), duplicateGame and deleteGame (which can bring back a game another editor deleted). Separately, pushConfig has no first-pull gate like remoteReady: an edit made between attaching fbConfigRef and the first config snapshot (for example after the auto-reload reopens the builder from state.ui.view) sends the device's cached, possibly days-old catalog over the server.
evidence: Ran config.js: two harness contexts using the real ensureGameDraft/saveGameDraft/applyRemoteConfig and the same stash-while-mid-entry logic as the fbConfigRef listener. Output: 'B builderDirty: true', 'server has Rain Relay after A saves: true', 'B stashed it (pendingRemoteConfig set): true', 'server has Rain Relay after B saves: false', 'A still has Rain Relay: false'.
fix: Add a helper in app.js, `rebaseOnPendingConfig()`: if pendingRemoteConfig is set, set state.config to it, run migrateState (with applyingRemoteConfig true), and clear it. Call it at the top of every builder commit before anything changes: saveGameDraft, duplicateGame, deleteGame, and each Days-tab handler (they already look things up by id when the event fires). Because the game editor keeps its edits in gameDraft, applying the newer config first and then splicing in only the edited game is safe. In saveGameDraft, if `!isNew` and the game no longer exists after the rebase, show 'This game was deleted by another editor' instead of saving. Also gate pushConfig on a `configReady` flag that the first fbConfigRef snapshot sets (including the `!remote` seed branch), mirroring remoteReady.

title: Two editors setting the same team's verse or cleanup points both get counted (for example 3 + 5 = 8)
scenario: setVersePoints (app.js:4596) and setCleanupPoints (app.js:4792) are meant to set a team's points for a day (and meal) to an exact value. Each one deletes the entries this device knows about and adds a new entry under a random newBonusId() (app.js:4604, 4801). Each bonus syncs under its own path, so two editors setting team t2's Monday verse at about the same time, or one editor whose device is holding off updates (still focused in a bonus or score input and then tapping a verse chip), each delete only what they've seen and each add their own entry. The server ends up with both, and t2's verse total in the standings and on the TV becomes the sum (3 + 5 = 8, above the 5-point chip maximum) until someone taps that row again.
evidence: Ran verse.js: two harness contexts, A runs setVersePoints('t2',1,3) and B runs setVersePoints('t2',1,5), then B takes the server snapshot. Output: the server bonuses hold two Monday-verse entries for t2 (3 and 5), and `medalCounts().t2.verse` = 8.
fix: Use fixed ids so the operation is idempotent: `const id = 'verse-' + teamId + '-' + dow` (cleanup: `'cleanup-' + teamId + '-' + dow + '-' + meal`). Delete any older entries for that team and day other than `id`, then set or delete `state.bonuses[id]`. Two devices then write the same path and end up with one value. If you want the change history to read 'changed 3 → 5' (IMPROVEMENTS #4), make describeCauses report a points change on the same id as 'changed'.

title: When a config change made elsewhere changes the points, every editor who has the app open logs it in the change history under their own name
scenario: Editor A ticks 'Double points' on a game that already has a result (or deletes a scored game, restores defaults, or imports a backup). On every other editor's device, applyRemoteConfig calls renderAll (app.js:2184) without setting remoteJustApplied. renderStandings then calls recordPointHistory(counts, false) (app.js:3871), and the `if (isRemote) return` guard (app.js:3971) doesn't apply. So each online editor's device writes changelog entries ('+7 Points updated') carrying its own byKey. The rules accept them because that editor really is the one writing. It also happens when an editor opens the app after such a change: the first config snapshot changes the totals compared with the cached baseline. The audit log ends up blaming the wrong people, and the entry is duplicated once per device.
evidence: Ran history.js: a harness context signed in as editor 'Bob', shields result saved, renderStandings baseline, then applyRemoteConfig with shields.messtival = true. Bob's device pushed three changelog entries (t0 +7, t1 +5, t2 +3), each with by 'Bob' and byKey 'bob@example,com'.
fix: In applyRemoteConfig, when `appStarted && JSON.stringify(state.config) !== beforeJson`, set `remoteJustApplied = true;` before calling renderAll(), the same way applyRemoteState does. The change is then treated as remote (pulse and notify, no log), and only the device that made the edit logs it, from its own saveConfig → renderAll.

title: Changing a started bracket game to another format leaves its bracket behind, and it shows as LIVE (or takes over the Big Board) on every home screen permanently
scenario: A ref taps Start Bracket on a 6-team tournament game, and then (rain, or a change of plan) a director switches the game to tally or placement in the builder. saveGameDraft only clears a saved result when the format changes (settings.js:787); state.brackets[gid] and the live tally stay. liveHomeGames (app.js:5083) counts any bracket not in 'summary' as live, without checking g.format or state.results. So every device keeps the game in 'Live now'. For tally, liveRankings defaults to on, and homeBoardGame puts it on the home Big Board ('Scoring under way…') even after its result is saved. No screen offers 'Cancel bracket' for a non-tournament game, so the only in-app way out is deleting the game, which also deletes its result.
evidence: node -e with the harness: freshBracket on musical-chairs, then the real saveGameDraft switching it to tally with liveRankings, then a saved result. Output: 'format now: tally', 'leftover bracket: true', 'liveHomeGames: ["musical-chairs"]', 'homeBoardGame (Big Board on every home screen): musical-chairs', 'gameStatus: done'.
fix: In saveGameDraft, when formatChanged, also delete state.brackets[out.id] and state.drafts[out.id] and call clearLiveMatch(existing) (extend the confirm to say an in-progress bracket or score entry is discarded). In liveHomeGames, only count the bracket branch when `g.format === 'tournament' && !state.results[g.id]`.

title: counterAllowNegative (Counselor Hide and Seek) doesn't work: negative scores are treated as 0, left out of rankings and dropped when the result is saved
