scenario: Counselor Hide and Seek is a double-points game configured with counterAllowNegative: true and a −1 button, and the builder exposes the option (gd-allownegative). The counter handler lets the score reach '-1' (app.js:5501), but it reads the current value back with parseScoreInput, which rejects any negative (app.js:3707) and falls back to 0 (app.js:5499). From −1, '−1' stays at −1 and '+1' jumps to 1 instead of 0. tallyRankLive/autoRank leave the team off the live board and the medal auto-fill, and the viewers' board never reaches 'n/n teams in · medals ready'. Save Result also drops the negative score from result.scores.
evidence: node -e with the harness on gameById('counselor-hide-seek'): the counter arithmetic gives 'tap -1 at -1 -> -1' and 'tap +1 at -1 -> 1', and with scores {t0:'-1', t1:'3', t2:'0'}, tallyRankLive and autoRank both return only t1 and t2.
fix: Allow negatives in parseScoreInput when the game permits them: `if (isNaN(v) || (v < 0 && !game.counterAllowNegative)) return null;` (and the same check in the mm:ss branch). Keep the scoring.test 'never negative' assertion for ordinary games and add a case for a game with counterAllowNegative.

title: If vendor/jelly.js fails to load or parse, the whole app goes invisible, including the sign-in buttons (always fails on iOS/iPadOS before 16.4)
scenario:
styles.css:130 sets `:not(:defined) { visibility: hidden; }` for every custom element. Only drawer, dialog, accordion, collapsible-header, tabs and progress get a degraded fallback (styles.css:138-157, 535-547, 697-701, 989). jelly-button and jelly-input get none. Every sign-in control is one of those two: index.html:86 (#google-signin-btn), :106-107 (retry/switch), auth-email-link.js:96-97 and auth-phone.js:85-90.

Path A, which always happens: vendor/jelly.js uses ES2022 class static initialization blocks. One sits in the base class L at vendor/jelly.js:872, and jelly-button extends L at :1362. There are 11 in total, plus unconditional `this.attachInternals()` calls at :1541, 1888 and others. Safari and iOS WebKit only support these from 16.4. On iPhone 6s/7/SE1 (capped at iOS 15.8), iPad Air 2 / mini 4 (iPadOS 15.8), or any device not updated past 16.3, the module throws a SyntaxError at parse time and no jelly-* element is ever defined. app.js and the other classic scripts use nothing newer than replaceAll (checked by grep), so the page itself runs. A signed-out user sees "Staff sign-in" with no button: an element with visibility:hidden cannot be clicked. The email and phone forms are invisible too. A returning approved device paints the app, but every card's content is hidden permanently by styles.css:546 (`jelly-collapsible:not(:defined) > :not([slot=header]) {display:none}`), so it shows only card headers.

Path B, flaky camp wifi on any device: the 312KB module fetch fails. That happens most often right after a deploy, when every phone auto-reloads at once and re-fetches the new ?v= URL. Module fetches are never retried, so the result is the same as Path A until a manual reload, and an installed home-screen app has no reload button.

It also makes the wait worse: boot runs on DOMContentLoaded (app.js:7971), and the spec makes DOMContentLoaded wait for a non-async module script. So a slow jelly.js fetch also holds back auth and sync start, despite the comment at index.html:57-59.
evidence: Ran `grep -nE "static \{" vendor/jelly.js`: 11 hits starting at 872. `grep -n attachInternals vendor/jelly.js`: 10 unconditional calls. `grep -n "not(:defined)" styles.css` shows no jelly-button or jelly-input fallback. Scanned app.js, settings.js, chat.js, camps.js, defaults.js and auth-*.js for post-Safari-15 syntax: only replaceAll (Safari 13.1+). index.html:60 loads the module, and the sign-in markup at :86, :106 and :107 uses only jelly-button. The test suite cannot see this because its DOM stub never evaluates CSS or the module.
fix:
Make the global hide time-limited instead of permanent.

(1) In styles.css, change line 130 to `html:not(.jelly-failed) :not(:defined) { visibility: hidden; }`. Add degraded rules under `html.jelly-failed`:
- `jelly-button:not(:defined) { display:inline-block; padding:.7em 1.2em; border:1px solid currentColor; border-radius:12px; cursor:pointer; text-align:center }` (use display:block for `[block]`)
- `jelly-collapsible:not(:defined) > :not([slot=header]) { display:block }`

(2) In boot-guard.js, which is classic and runs after the module tag is parsed:
- attach an 'error' listener to `document.querySelector('script[src*="vendor/jelly.js"]')` to catch a network failure
- add a `window.addEventListener('error', e => /jelly\.js/.test(e.filename || '') && …)` handler to catch the parse error
- add a ~4s `setTimeout` fallback that checks `customElements.get('jelly-button')`
- each of these adds `jelly-failed` to documentElement

An undefined jelly-button still receives the click listeners app.js attaches, so Google sign-in works once the button is visible.

(3) Optionally, so iOS 15 gets the real UI: mechanically rewrite jelly.js's 11 `static { this.X = v; }` blocks to `static X = v;` (static fields work from Safari 14.1), and change `this.attachInternals()` to `this.attachInternals?.()`. Re-test on an iOS 15 device.

title: TV page: clicking "Continue with Google" (or pressing Space/Enter on it) starts the reveal with no data, and the TV stays blank until someone reloads
scenario:
A signed-out TV shows #auth-overlay. The click on #auth-ov-btn opens the popup (:711-718), then bubbles to the document click handler at :1053. That handler only ignores `.topbar` and calls advance(). With phase 'intro', beginReveal() (:916) sets `phase='reveal'`, freezes `order = (liveGroups || []).slice().reverse()` (:921) to [] because no data has loaded yet, hides the intro, and calls showBig(0). That throws at :811-812 (`order[0].entries`) with bigIndex already set to 0.

After the popup succeeds, the data loads and onDataReady shows the screen, but the intro is gone and `order` stays []. The presenter's taps then go: TypeError, then finish(), then an empty final table. The TV shows a blank white stage at showtime.

The update auto-reload cannot fix it because it only reloads in phase 'intro' (:1077). Keyboard sign-in is broken outright: the keydown handler at :1045 calls preventDefault on Space/Enter, so the focused button never activates, and it runs the same advance().

This is the designed path for every TV sign-in: first setup, and again after Safari's 7-day storage purge, which the comment at :654-656 expects.
evidence: Loaded the real inline script from current-standings.html into a Node vm with a DOM stub and a firebase stub (scratchpad tvclick2.js). Steps: auth callback(null), then a document click, then auth callback(user), then a state snapshot, then 4 presenter taps. Output: "sign-in click → advance() threw: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'entries')" / "data ready; loading hidden: true | intro hidden: true" / tap 1 threw the same / taps 2-4 ok with hero="" and board="".
fix:
Ignore input until there is data to reveal, and keep the state machine untouched on a bad start.
- Click handler: `if (!haveData || e.target.closest('.topbar, #auth-overlay')) return;`
- Keydown handler: `if (!haveData || document.getElementById('auth-overlay').style.display !== 'none') return;` before preventDefault.
- beginReveal(): guard `if (!liveGroups || !liveGroups.length) return;` before setting `phase = 'reveal'`.

title: TV page: data listeners have no cancel callback and are never re-attached, so after an auth change the TV silently shows frozen standings
scenario:
attachData() attaches `.on('value')` to campScoreboard/config (:679) and campScoreboard/state (:686) with no cancel callback. It runs once, guarded by `started` (:735).

The presenter laptop typically also has the main app open, because the TV is reached via Settings → Stalling → Current Standings. Suppose someone signs out or switches account in the main app tab (signOutAndClear). Firebase Auth syncs the null user to the TV tab, and the TV's onAuthStateChanged shows the sign-in overlay (:724). RTDB re-evaluates rules under the new null auth and revokes both listens. Without a cancel callback this is only a console warning, and the SDK never re-arms a revoked listen (CLAUDE.md's 'terminal read' invariant).

The presenter signs back in. The members once() approves and hides the overlay (:734), but `started` is already true, so nothing re-attaches. The TV looks healthy but never updates again, and the reveal shows whatever standings existed at sign-out.

Any other revocation lands in the same silent state. The main app avoids this by reloading after teardown, a one-shot lifecycle the TV never adopted.
evidence: Read current-standings.html:671-739. Both `.on()` calls take only a success callback. `started` is never reset. No `location.reload()` happens on an auth transition. Compare app.js, whose sign-out and re-sign-in paths both end in location.reload(), as documented in CLAUDE.md under 'One-shot lifecycle'.
fix:
Use the main app's one-shot lifecycle:
- In onAuthStateChanged, `if (!user || !user.email) { if (started) { location.reload(); return; } setAuthOverlay('signin'); return; }`.
- Pass a cancel callback to both `.on()` calls in attachData, e.g. `function () { setAuthOverlay('denied', ...); setTimeout(reloadNow, 5000); }` so a revoked listen is visible and recovers.

This cannot loop: a reload that is still denied stops at the once() check and never attaches.

title: Announcement composer: the 30-second tick rebuilds it and erases the text an editor is typing
scenario:
An editor taps "📣 Post an announcement" and starts typing in #announce-input. The 30s setInterval at app.js:7361 calls `renderAnnouncements()` unconditionally. renderAnnouncements rebuilds the whole strip with `wrap.innerHTML = banners + composer` (:6977), which recreates an empty <input id=announce-input>. The typed text is lost, focus drops and the phone keyboard closes.

Typing a sentence on a phone takes 10-40 s, so most announcements cross a tick. The code already knows a re-render wipes the input: the comment at ~:6990 says the TTL chips flip in place for exactly that reason. editorMidEntry() protects remote merges but not this timer. This is outside the shell subsystem, but it is solid and cheap to fix.
evidence: Harness simulation (scratchpad announce.js): with setMemberRole('editor') and announceComposerOpen=true, I seeded the input with typed text, then ran the interval body `pruneExpiredAnnouncements(); renderAnnouncements();`. The output showed the composer HTML rebuilt with no value ("composer rebuilt (typed text gone): true"). renderAnnouncements has no activeElement or draft guard.
fix:
In renderAnnouncements, before rebuilding:
- read `const prev = document.getElementById('announce-input'); const draft = prev ? prev.value : ''; const hadFocus = prev && document.activeElement === prev;`
- after the innerHTML assignment, restore the value, and if hadFocus, focus the input and put the caret at the end.

Alternatively, render banners and composer into two child containers and rebuild the composer only when announceComposerOpen changes.

title: TV standings count orphaned results that the main app ignores, so the reveal can show different totals and order
scenario:
app.js medalCounts() skips any result whose game id is no longer in the live config (`const g = gameById(id); if (!g) return;`, app.js:3757-3758). CLAUDE.md lists this as a scoring invariant, and scoring.test.js pins it.

computeStandings in current-standings.html (:430-441) counts every `state.results` entry, using the config only for the ×2 flag.

An orphan reaches the live state through the two-editors race: editor A deletes game X in the week builder (settings.js:853 deletes results[X], then a config push and a state push), while editor B, not yet holding A's config, saves X's podium. B's per-path diff writes state/results/X back. Nothing prunes it remotely, because pruneOrphanedGameData only runs on import and restore. The phones then rank without X, and the TV reveal ranks with it.
evidence: Loaded app.js via tests/harness.js and the TV's computeStandings from the real HTML into a separate vm (scratchpad tvparity.js). I used the same remote state: 2 real results plus 1 orphan. Output: TV `t0=12 t1=12 t2=10 t3=8 t4=3 t5=0` vs APP `t0=12 t1=12 t2=3 t3=3 t4=0 t5=0`. The 3rd/4th/5th places differ.
fix: In updateDoubledFrom, also record `liveGameIds = new Set(arr.map(g => g && g.id).filter(Boolean))`. In computeStandings's results loop, add `if (liveGameIds && !liveGameIds.has(id)) return;`, mirroring medalCounts. Recompute when the config lands; that already happens at :681-683.

title: TV page treats phone-number accounts as signed out and only mirrors emailKey, not identityKey
scenario:
Members can be keyed by phone (app.js identityKey, :179-184, CLAUDE.md 'Identity is email OR phone'). The TV's onAuthStateChanged returns early with the sign-in overlay when `!user.email` (:724), and builds its key with the email transform only (:729).

An approved phone-only director whose browser session is a phone account opens the TV. Firebase auth state is shared per origin with the main app. The TV says "Staff sign-in", and the only way forward is a Google sign-in. That replaces the origin's session in the main app tab too. The emailKey copy itself does match app.js (trim, lowercase, replaceAll).
evidence: Compared current-standings.html:724-731 with app.js:158-184. The email transform is identical; the phone branch is missing.
fix: Mirror identityKey. If user.email exists, use the existing email key. Otherwise, if user.phoneNumber exists, use it as the key (Firebase already reports it in E.164). Only show 'signin' when neither exists.

title: sw.js notificationclick focuses whichever same-origin window was used last, often the TV or stalling tab instead of the scoreboard
scenario:
maybeNativeNotification (app.js:2872) only notifies when the scoreboard tab is hidden, which means another window is in front. On the presenter laptop that is typically current-standings.html or stalling.html. Both are inside the SW scope './' (manifest.json scope, register('sw.js') at app.js:7354).

On click, `wins.find((w) => 'focus' in w)` picks the first WindowClient. Every WindowClient has focus, and matchAll lists the most recently focused first, so it picks the TV tab that is already in front. Nothing visible happens and the scoreboard never comes forward.

This matters more once the planned push handler lands in sw.js (PROGRESS.md).
evidence: Read sw.js:24-32 and app.js:2872-2890. The TV and stalling pages live in the same directory, so the registration controls them too.
fix: Prefer the app window: `const isApp = (w) => { const p = new URL(w.url).pathname; return p.endsWith('/') || p.endsWith('/index.html'); }; const win = wins.find(isApp);`. Then `return win ? win.focus() : self.clients.openWindow('./');`.

title: A result saved offline is silently lost when the page reloads before the server acknowledges it (the deploy auto-reload doesn't wait, and the next load's first snapshot overwrites it)
scenario: 1) An editor saves a placement or tally result on flaky camp wifi. saveState writes it to localStorage (app.js:1974). pushState calls fbRef.update(), which the SDK queues in memory only, so pendingWrites=1 (app.js:2604). After the push, dataEditPending=false and pushTimer=null. The indicator promises "Offline — will sync when back". 2) A reload happens before the server acknowledges the write. Two realistic causes: (a) The owner deploys, which happened 13–19 times a day during camp week. On the next visibilitychange or 2-minute poll, checkForUpdate → onNewVersion → reloadWhenSafe (app.js:7174). reloadWhenSafe checks only editorMidEntry() (app.js:7075-7091), which looks at focus, dataEditPending, pushTimer and pushConfigTimer but not pendingWrites. It reloads 1.2s later, typically while the woken phone is still refreshing its expired ID token and reconnecting RTDB. (b) iOS evicts the backgrounded home-screen app. The RTDB web SDK has no disk persistence, so the queued write is gone. 3) The new page loads the result from localStorage, but dirtySinceLoad is an in-memory flag that starts false (app.js:2121). It is set only by saves made in this load before the first snapshot (app.js:1972). So handleRemoteSnapshot skips the offline-work defense (app.js:2306) and applyRemoteState replaces state.results with the server copy. It also writes that copy to localStorage, so the result disappears from the device too. No error is shown.
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/reloadloss.js, which loads the real files through a copy of tests/harness.js that can pre-seed storage. Session 1 used an fbRef whose update() never resolves, then saved a result for 'shields'. Output: "queued in SDK memory: 1 | pendingWrites: 1" and "editorMidEntry() = false". Session 2 started a fresh context with Session 1's localStorage: "result in local state? true | dirtySinceLoad = false". After handleRemoteSnapshot(serverTree): "result still there? false | pushed: 0" and "localStorage still has it? false". /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/reloaddemo.js shows that with pendingWrites=1, reloadWhenSafe() schedules ["doReload@1200"]. git log shows 19, 18 and 13 commits (deploys) on 2026-07-24/25/26.
fix: (a) Stop-gap, one line in reloadWhenSafe (app.js:7175): `if (!canEdit() || (!editorMidEntry() && pendingWrites === 0)) { setTimeout(doReload, 1200); return; }`. The update banner already lets the user refresh by hand. (b) Root cause: save the last server-confirmed baseline with the snapshot. Write `lastSyncedTree` to `lsKey('campScoreboardSyncBase')` in applyRemoteState after `lastSyncedTree = syncedSnapshot()`, and in pushState's success settle when pendingWrites drops to 0. Read it at load into `persistedSyncBase`. In handleRemoteSnapshot's first-snapshot path, when persistedSyncBase exists: compute `unsynced = computeSyncUpdates(persistedSyncBase, syncedSnapshot())` before adopting, call applyRemoteState(remote), re-apply each `unsynced` path from the pre-adopt local copy onto state, then call saveState(). That schedules the normal per-path push against the new baseline. Add 'campScoreboardSyncBase' to the clearLocalData bases list and add a sync.test case for it. Avoid simply persisting dirtySinceLoad: that path does a whole-tree first push (lastSyncedTree is null), and it would revert other refs' newer drafts, live tallies and clocks, which never advance meta.lastDataChangeAt.

title: If the Firebase SDK fails to load, a returning editor gets an editable app that never syncs, never retries, and only says so inside a collapsed card
scenario: The three gstatic Firebase scripts are separate cross-origin requests from index.html and app.js. On flaky camp wifi one can fail while the same-origin page loads. Then boot() (app.js:7972) runs on a device with a cached hint: setMemberRole('editor') and startApp() (app.js:7991-7993). startAuth() reaches the `typeof firebase === 'undefined' || !firebase.auth` branch (app.js:7638). Its comment says "run local-only, view-only", but it only calls startApp() and never clears the hinted editor role. The editor can score games, and each save goes only to localStorage (fbRef is null, so schedulePush returns). Nothing retries: there is no 'online' listener anywhere in app.js, and only a version bump reloads. The only signal is "📱 This device only" (app.js:2711) in #sync-status, which sits inside the Standings card (index.html:199). applyCardDefaults (app.js:7540) collapses that card on every load. When the phone later reloads with the SDK, those results are erased by the first-snapshot path in the high-severity finding above. A device with no hint (a counselor's first visit) skips the sign-in screen and shows a default, empty "no scores yet" scoreboard as if it were real.
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/nosdk.js with harness storage seeded `campScoreboardAuthHint='editor'`, FIREBASE_CONFIG={apiKey:'x',…} and no `firebase` global, then called boot(). Output: "appStarted: true | canEdit(): true | syncEnabled(): false | syncStarted: false". A saved result then lands only in localStorage ("result saved locally: true | fbRef: null"). grep for 'online' and navigator.onLine in app.js and chat.js found nothing.
fix: In startAuth (app.js:7636), split the branch. `if (!cfg || !cfg.apiKey) { startApp(); return; }` stays the true local-dev path. When cfg.apiKey is set but the SDK is missing, treat it as a load failure: if a hinted app is already painted, call setMemberRole('viewer') so the cached copy is read-only. Otherwise call showAuthScreen('signin', { error: "Couldn't reach the sign-in service — check your connection." }) rather than startApp(). Set a `sdkMissing` flag so updateSyncIndicator shows '⚠️ Couldn't connect — read-only copy', and show a one-time toast, since the chip is in a collapsed card. Arrange a retry: `window.addEventListener('online', doReload, { once: true })`, plus a reload on visibilitychange→visible throttled by a sessionStorage timestamp (at most one per 60s) so it can't loop.

title: In any chat channel with 50+ messages, every incoming message wipes the text being typed and dismisses the keyboard
scenario: Each channel listens with limitToLast(CHAT_WINDOW=50) (chat.js:28, chat.js:112) and has a child_removed handler (chat.js:119). Once a channel holds 50 or more messages (General will within the first day of camp), each new message from anyone makes RTDB fire child_removed for the oldest message as it slides out of the window. onChatMsgRemoved then calls renderChatView(true) (chat.js:160) while the user is viewing that channel. The forced rebuild reassigns view.innerHTML (chat.js:838), which recreates `<input id="chat-input">` (chat.js:851) with no value. The half-typed message is lost, focus drops, the iOS keyboard closes, and the list jumps to the bottom. This contradicts the stated design that the view rebuilds only on open or channel switch so the composer never loses text. The same forced rebuild runs on every members snapshot via onMemberDirectoryChanged (chat.js:219-222).
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/chatwipe.js, which loads the real files through the harness. It opens General with 50 messages, sets #chat-view's innerHTML to a sentinel standing for the user's built view, then calls onChatMsgRemoved('general',{key:'m000'}) as RTDB does on a window slide. Output: "view rebuilt by child_removed: true | new composer markup: <input type=\"text\" id=\"chat-input\" … autocomplete=\"off\">" (no value). grep finds no draft preservation in chat.js.
fix: Make onChatMsgRemoved remove the one bubble instead of rebuilding. Find the `.chat-bubble` in #chat-list whose dataset.msgId === snap.key and remove it, along with a `.chat-day-sep` left with no bubble after it. Fall back to renderChatView(true) only when the element isn't found. Also make renderChatView keep the composer whenever it rebuilds the same channel. Before `view.innerHTML = …`, capture the old #chat-input value, selectionStart and whether it was document.activeElement (only when chatViewBuiltFor === ch), and restore them after wireChatView. That also covers onMemberDirectoryChanged and toggleChatSub.

title: The deploy auto-reload discards a chat message being typed or a photo still uploading, for every user
scenario: reloadWhenSafe reloads viewers unconditionally (`!canEdit() ||`). For editors, it excludes the chat composer from editorMidEntry on purpose (app.js:7084-7086, so chat focus doesn't block sync). The chat itself is open to all members. With 13–19 deploys a day during camp week, every open phone reloads 1.2s after its next poll or refocus. Someone typing a long message, or in the few seconds while sendChatPhoto (chat.js:296) compresses and uploads a photo through chatAtomicSend, is reloaded mid-action. The text, or the photo send, is lost without explanation. sendChatMessage clears the input before the ack (chat.js:275), and its give-the-words-back recovery (chat.js:280) cannot run after a reload.
evidence: Read reloadWhenSafe (app.js:7174-7177) and editorMidEntry (app.js:7075-7091). /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/reloaddemo.js puts an editor's focus in a #chat-view input with pendingWrites=0. reloadWhenSafe() still schedules ["doReload@1200"]; for a viewer the canEdit() short-circuit reloads with no check at all.
fix: Add `chatBusy()` to chat.js. It returns true when #chat-input has non-blank text or a send is in flight; keep a `chatSendsInFlight` counter incremented in sendChatMessage and sendChatPhoto and decremented when chatAtomicSend settles. Gate the reload for everyone, not just editors: `const busy = (canEdit() && editorMidEntry()) || pendingWrites > 0 || (typeof chatBusy === 'function' && chatBusy()); if (!busy) { setTimeout(doReload, 1200); return; } setTimeout(reloadWhenSafe, 12000);`. The update banner already gives a manual refresh.

title: Pictionary photo store keeps a dead IndexedDB connection forever and treats a write as saved before it commits
scenario: photoDB() (app.js:3116-3126) caches its promise permanently. An open error, or a connection the browser closes (iOS WebKit's "Connection to Indexed Database server lost" after the phone is backgrounded between teams), leaves every later putPhoto/getPhoto failing on the same cached db until a full reload. Each attempt shows "Could not save that photo — try again." (app.js:3444), but trying again cannot work. Separately, idbOp (app.js:3128-3135) resolves on the request's onsuccess rather than tx.oncomplete. A readwrite transaction that aborts at commit, such as QuotaExceededError on a phone with nearly full storage, still resolves. The caller then sets laps[i].photo = true and syncs it (app.js:3439-3440), and exportTeamPhotos later skips the missing blob silently (`if (!blob) continue`).
evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/idbdemo.js against the real files with a stubbed indexedDB. With a db whose transaction() throws UnknownError, three putPhoto attempts all rejected and "indexedDB.open calls so far: 1" never changed. With a put request that succeeds followed by a QuotaExceededError abort at commit, putPhoto returned "RESOLVED (caller sets laps[1].photo = true)".
fix: In idbOp, wrap `db.transaction` in try/catch. Resolve readwrite operations on `tx.oncomplete` with the request's result, and reject on `tx.onabort`/`tx.onerror` with tx.error. On any failure set `photoDBPromise = null` before rejecting, so the next attempt reopens; optionally retry once inside idbOp. In photoDB's onsuccess, add `db.onclose = db.onversionchange = () => { try { db.close(); } catch (e) {} photoDBPromise = null; };`, and also null the memo in req.onerror.
